distractors: To hold a connection open between requests so that the next one does not pay again for setting it up.
To keep a copy close to whoever is asking so that repeat reads come back fast, on the understanding that the copy is disposable and can be rebuilt from source whenever it is wrong.

To take a copy to a second location on a schedule so that there is something to restore from if the first one is lost. Nobody reads from that copy while things are going well, which is why it is so often found broken.

To flatten a structure into a run of bytes so that it can cross a network and be rebuilt into the same shape at the other end. The concern is the format on the wire, and both sides have to agree on it before anything useful moves.

To keep two systems in agreement as records change on either side, applying an agreed rule to decide which version wins when both of them moved at the same moment. Almost all of the work is in the reconciliation rather than in the writing, and almost all of the bugs are there too.
The ability to come back quickly after a setback, more or less as you were before it.
A willingness to take on the work nobody else wants, usually because it is dull rather than because it is difficult.
Refusing to move from a position even once the evidence against it has been laid out, which reads as conviction from the inside and as obstinacy from anywhere else.
Care and attention to detail held at the same level over long stretches of work, so that the last page gets exactly the treatment the first one did, long after anybody would notice if it had not.

Confidence that a plan will come good in spite of what the people around you think, held firmly enough that you carry on funding it out of your own budget. It is a judgement about the odds, and it is either vindicated in the end or it is not.
